dialog.body: Public Works, this is Lorraine. How can I help you?
Yes, hi, um, this is Linh Goldberg, I'm on Marsh Street, and well, I am beyond fed up. The drain in front of my house is flooding again, and this has been going on for weeks. Weeks.
I'm sorry, Ms. Goldberg. Let me get some details. What's the address on Marsh Street?

One forty-one Marsh Street, down the Point. Um, it's right at the curb by my driveway. The grate has sunk, like it's actually lower than the pavement around it, and, well, the water goes everywhere but down it. It runs right across the sidewalk and into my garage.
One forty-one Marsh Street, and the grate at the curb has sunk down. Did this happen with the rain from Friday into Saturday?

Yes! Yesterday, all day, it just poured and the street turned into a pond. Um, and the garage flooded. I had furniture stored in there, a dresser, two chairs, a table I was going to refinish, and it's all ruined. Soaked through. Swollen. Garbage now.
Oh, that's awful. So the water came into the garage from the street, and the stored furniture is damaged. Let me write that down.

And I'm not the first time calling about the, um, the general problem. It's the same thing every time it rains. Nobody comes, nobody looks, and meanwhile I'm out the furniture. I'm telling you, if nothing happens this week I'm calling the TV news. I will call the station and let them stand in my driveway.
I understand you're upset, and I do want to get this in front of the right people. Can I ask what you'd like done? Is it the drain cleaned out?

Yes. Clean it out. Clean the drain, check the grate, fix the grate, whatever it takes. It's full of leaves and sand and muck, and well, the thing is sunk so even if it were clean the water wouldn't go in properly. Somebody needs to actually look at it.

Okay. So I'm putting down: storm drain at the curb in front of 141 Marsh Street, grate sunk below the road surface, debris in it, requesting cleaning and an inspection of the grate. Water running into the garage. Is that right?
That's right. That's it exactly. And put that it's been weeks. Not one day. Weeks.
I'll note that it's an ongoing problem, not just from this storm. Is the water still standing there today?

Some of it, yeah, there's a puddle by the curb, the rest drained off, well, drained into my yard mostly. Sorry, I'm loud, I know, I'm just, um, I'm really angry. I've got a batch of kombucha brewing in the pantry and I'm standing here in the kitchen shouting over it.
You're fine, I can hear you okay. Is this the best number to reach you, the one you're calling from?
Yes, it's four-oh-one, five-five-five, oh-one-seven-nine.

Four-oh-one, five-five-five, oh-one-seven-nine. Got it. Since it's Sunday, the request will go in the queue and the crew supervisor will see it first thing Monday. I can't tell you the exact day a crew will get out there, but this will be logged with the sunken grate and the garage flooding.
Monday. Okay. Well, I'm going to hold you to Monday for somebody at least looking at it. Because I'm not kidding about the news.
I hear you, Ms. Goldberg. I've noted how serious it is. If you have photos of the grate and the garage, keep them handy in case someone asks.
Oh, I have plenty. Believe me. I took them yesterday, standing in the water.
Good. Then you're all set on my end. Someone from Public Works should be in touch. Anything else I can help with today?
No. That's it. Just, please, get it fixed. Thank you.
You're welcome. Take care, and I hope the rest of your Sunday gets better.
